title: Left derived functor via K-flat resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal abelian category with the following properties: its
tensor product is additive in each variable; it has countable coproducts and exact
$\mathbf Z$-indexed colimits, which tensoring with a fixed object on either side
preserves; and it has functorial flat resolutions. Let $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$
be an additive functor to an abelian category that preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms
[def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. The *left derived functor*
$LF\colon D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ is the total left derived functor of
$K(\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{F}K(\mathcal D)\xrightarrow{Q}D(\mathcal D)$ with respect to
the quasi-isomorphisms. It comes with a counit $LF\circ Q\Rightarrow Q\circ F$, which is
an isomorphism on K-flat complexes. So $LF(K)=F(P)$ for a K-flat resolution $P\to K$.
Conversely, a functor with a counit is the left derived functor if and only if its counit
is an isomorphism on all K-flat complexes.

Here monoidal and abelian categories are as in [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and [def-sp-abelian], and the coproducts and colimits are those of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; $\mathbf Z$ is ordered by $\leq$, not discrete, for the latter colimits. Exactness of this colimit functor means preservation of short exact sequences. A flat object is one whose two fixed-factor tensor functors preserve short exact sequences; functorial flat resolutions mean a functor $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ with flat values and a natural epimorphism $P\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}$. Complexes, quasi-isomorphisms and the localizations $Q_{\mathcal C},Q_{\mathcal D}$ are those of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The homotopy category has complexes as objects and cochain maps modulo $f-g=dh+hd$ as morphisms. The total left derived universal property means that composition with the counit gives, for every $V:D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$, a bijection $\operatorname{Nat}(V,LF)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(V\circ Q_{\mathcal C},Q_{\mathcal D}\circ F)$, where these two occurrences of $Q$ have source the homotopy categories. The displayed resolution formula denotes a canonical isomorphism $LF(Q_{\mathcal C}K)\cong Q_{\mathcal D}(FP)$.

proof.text: Put $A=K(\mathcal C)$, let $W$ be its quasi-isomorphisms, and let $i:\mathcal P\hookrightarrow A$ be the full subcategory of K-flat complexes. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-sequential-kflat-derivability] are precisely the hypotheses on $\mathcal C$: flatness is two-sided, the colimits are indexed by the ordered integers, and no Grothendieck, symmetry or closedness assumption is needed. It supplies a left derivability structure for $i$ with $W_{\mathcal P}=i^{-1}W$. The localization $Q_{\mathcal C}:A\to D(\mathcal C)$ is the homotopy-category localization specified by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If the preservation phrase in the statement is read as referring only to ordered-integer colimits, countable-coproduct preservation still follows: a countable coproduct is the colimit of its increasing finite partial biproducts, extended by zero to negative integer stages. Maps out of this colimit are exactly families of maps from its summands. An additive tensor functor preserves each finite biproduct and, by hypothesis, this integer colimit, hence preserves their countable coproduct. In Lean, preservation of countable coproducts is proved by the final functor Int.toNat from the ordered integers to the naturals, followed by the final sequential functor to the countable directed preorder of finite subsets of the index set. Express the coproduct as the colimit of its finite subcoproducts. Additivity makes the finite coproduct comparison maps invertible, and preservation of the directed colimit makes the full coproduct comparison invertible. These preservation instances supply the graded tensor coherence hypotheses in the existing source K-flat derivability theorem. The two-sided binary-total-tensor predicate agrees definitionally with the source monoidal K-flat predicate.

source.place: Opening sentence: K-flat left derivability; the colimit hypotheses are checked explicitly

proof.text: Apply $F$ termwise to cochain complexes and cochain maps. Additivity gives $F(0)=0$ on morphisms, so $F(d^{n+1})F(d^n)=0$. It also carries a homotopy equation $f-g=dh+hd$ to $F(f)-F(g)=F(d)F(h)+F(h)F(d)$, so it induces $F_h:K(\mathcal C)\to K(\mathcal D)$. Set $G=Q_{\mathcal D}\circ F_h$. For any arrow $s$ in $W_{\mathcal P}$, both endpoints are K-flat and $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The preservation property [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] says exactly that $F(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism; localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore makes $G(s)$ invertible. This verifies the restriction-inverts-$W_{\mathcal P}$ hypothesis, without requiring $F$ to be exact or its values to be K-flat.

source.place: Middle sentences: the functor-specific preservation hypothesis, made explicit on the homotopy quotient

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-unary-left-derived-calculus] with $A=K(\mathcal C)$, $D=D(\mathcal C)$, $H=D(\mathcal D)$, $L=Q_{\mathcal C}$, resolving inclusion $i$ from step 1, and functor $G$ from step 2. Quasi-isomorphisms contain identities by their cohomology definition. All hypotheses have now been verified. The theorem supplies $(LF,\varepsilon)$ with $\varepsilon:LF\circ Q_{\mathcal C}\Rightarrow G$ and, for every $V$, the bijection $\operatorname{Nat}(V,LF)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(V\circ Q_{\mathcal C},G)$. Define the left derived functor to be this universally characterized functor with its counit. The same cited statement says that, for every candidate $(T,\eta)$, this universal property holds if and only if every $\eta_{iP}$ is invertible. Applied to $(LF,\varepsilon)$ it gives invertibility on all K-flat complexes; applied to arbitrary $(T,\eta)$ it is exactly the final characterization in the item. Thus existence and the characterization use the general theorem, rather than an unjustified descent of a functor from a subcategory.

source.place: Last four sentences: construction by the derived universal property and the counit criterion

proof.text: For any given quasi-isomorphism q:P→K with P K-flat, Q_C(q) is invertible by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the counit at P is invertible by step 3. Apply LF to the inverse of Q_C(q), compose with the inverse of the canonical quotientCompQhIso at P, then with the counit at the homotopy image of P, and finally with quotientCompQhIso at F(P). This gives the asserted isomorphism LF(Q_C K) ≅ Q_D(F(P)). No separate resolution-existence theorem is needed for this conditional formula: existence already enters through the derivability structure in step 1.
